    ping 192.168.8.40

  2. Check service status: 

    ssh remote@192.168.8.40
systemctl --user status goblin-video.service

  3. Check logs: 

    journalctl --user -u goblin-video.service -f

  4. Restart service: 

    systemctl --user restart goblin-video.service

docs.title: Videos Not Playing
docs.text:
1. Verify video exists: 

    ssh remote@192.168.8.40
ls -lh /home/remote/media/video/

  2. Check MPV process: 

    ps aux | grep mpv

  3. Test MPV directly: 

    mpv --vo=drm --drm-connector=HDMI-A-1 /home/remote/media/video/test.mp4

  4. Check video format: 

    ffprobe /home/remote/media/video/test.mp4

docs.title: CORS Errors

  3. Redeploy if missing:

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
This document provides a comprehensive audit of the Express middleware configuration for the MonsterBox application, identifying security vulnerabilities, performance bottlenecks, and optimization opportunities.

Audit Date: 2025-06-16 Auditor: TaskMaster AI System Status: ✅ COMPLETED - All recommendations implemented

docs.title: Helmet Security Headers
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Implemented with custom CSP
  • Configuration:
  • Content Security Policy configured for WebSocket and WebRTC support
  • Cross-Origin Embedder Policy disabled for WebRTC compatibility
  • Font and style sources configured for Google Fonts

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Implemented with dual-tier approach
  • General Limiter: 1000 requests per 15 minutes per IP
  • API Limiter: 500 API requests per 15 minutes per IP
  • Features: Standard headers, legacy headers disabled

docs.title: JSON Parser
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Enhanced with security limits
  • Limit: 10MB maximum payload size
  • Strict Mode: Enabled for better parsing

docs.title: URL-Encoded Parser
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Enhanced with security limits
  • Limit: 10MB maximum payload size
  • Parameter Limit: 1000 parameters (prevents parameter pollution)

docs.title: Express Session
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Properly configured
  • Secret: Environment variable with secure fallback
  • Settings:
  • resave: false (optimal performance)
  • saveUninitialized: true (required for character selection)
  • Cookie security prepared for HTTPS

docs.title: JWT Integration
docs.text:
• Status: ✅ Properly integrated with session
  • Middleware: authMiddleware.integrateWithSession
  • Character Context: Global character selection middleware

docs.title: Custom Error Classes

  • AuthenticationError: 401 status for auth failures
  • AuthorizationError: 403 status for permission denials
  • NotFoundError: 404 status for missing resources

  • HardwareError: 503 status for hardware failures

Kept for reference, not loaded as commands.

  • build-v9-orlok.md, finish-ai-voices.md — mission commands scoped to the v9.0/v9.1 milestones. Both shipped; the repo is past v10.4.0 and heading for v11, and their step lists reference a mission doc and a state of the tree that no longer exist.
  • learn-monsterbox.md — "read everything up front" onboarding. Superseded by the progressive-disclosure layout: a lean CLAUDE.md plus topic skills that load when their topic actually comes up. Reading the whole repo into context before knowing the task is the specific pattern the Claude 5 context-engineering guidance names as counterproductive.

Restore any of these with git checkout on an older revision, or just move the file back up one directory.

docs.title: Build v9.0 — Orlok (autonomous)
docs.text: Execute the v9.0 Orlok build mission fully autonomously — do not ask the operator anything, do not pause for approval, do not present plans for sign-off. Decide, act, self-verify, and keep working until the Definition of Done is met.

docs.title: Step 1 — Familiarize
docs.text: Read, completely: 1. CLAUDE.md — rules, architecture constraints, code style, testing protocol. 2. The auto-loaded MEMORY.md and any relevant topic memory files. 3. docs/development/V9-ORLOK-MISSION.md — the authoritative mission (objective, rules, phases, Definition of Done). 4. docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md — the single fleet issue tracker (Orlok section + audit appendix).

docs.title: Step 2 — Confirm you are on Orlok
docs.text: Verify this node is Orlok (char_id 3). Check config/app-config.json / hostname; the fleet roster is in config/animatronics.json. If this is NOT the Orlok node, stop and say so — this mission drives real Orlok hardware and must run on that node.

docs.title: Step 3 — Execute the mission
docs.text:
Run docs/development/V9-ORLOK-MISSION.md end-to-end: Phase 0 (sync) → Phase 1 (organize issues) → Phase 2 (confirm toolchain) → Phase 3 (build to the v9.0 Definition of Done). Orchestrate the expert subagents in .claude/agents/ (hardware-diagnostician, python-wrapper-specialist, elevenlabs-ai-specialist, pose-author, test-runner, security-triager, docs-scribe, character-auditor) — the orchestrator–worker pattern — fanning out independent work in parallel and adversarially self-verifying results.

Honor every non-negotiable rule in the mission: no new dependencies/transports; hardware safety self-enforced (ch4/ch5 speed caps + serialization + safety layer BEFORE moving them; never retract part 3 below min); preserve node-local runtime state; the npm run gate is the guardrail and is run before every push; version comes only from package.json; commit small and push over SSH.

Do not stop until v9.0 is shipped (tagged, pushed, and verified end-to-end on real hardware).

docs.title: Finish AI Voices — v9.1 integration & test
docs.text:
Phase 0 — get oriented first. Run the /learn-monsterbox onboarding (or follow its steps manually): read CLAUDE.md end to end, the shared memory files (MEMORY.md and the elevenlabs-agent-fleet-tuning memory), and git log --oneline -40 — the v9.0.0 refactor landed alongside this milestone, so absorb both streams before touching anything. Also review the current Claude Code setup: .claude/commands/ and .claude/skills/ (available slash commands), .claude/agents/ (the expert subagent team — use character-auditor before any cross-character change, hardware-diagnostician for the audio work, test-runner for suites), and .mcp.json (Playwright MCP; the ElevenLabs MCP connector must be authenticated to the MonsterBox workspace — verify with an agents list before trusting it). Only then begin.

Fully integrate and verify the AI-voices milestone (git tag ai-voices-2026-08-16) against the current codebase for the v9.1 build. The newest ElevenLabs techniques and agent shapes are already in this repo: agent config snapshots in config/elevenlabs/ (with restore README), the full session record in docs/development/HALLOWEEN-TUNING-REPORT.md, and transcripts in docs/development/CONVERSATION-SAMPLES.md. Treat the snapshots as the canonical persona state — never regress an agent below its committed snapshot.

Work every §6 open item in HALLOWEEN-TUNING-REPORT.md to done:

  1. Fleet audio ear-check (the blocker). A microphone must exist first (this node's webcam mic was disconnected; its dongle jack was empty). Then run the instrumented cast test — TTS-cast every character per node while recording, measure dB, transcribe with Scribe — and produce a per-node audible/silent matrix. Fix what's silent (mixer, sink routing, cabling notes for the human). Verify Orlok's 0.75 TTS speed and each v3 voice by ear; adjust only with reason.

  2. Renfield's node online. Hardware exists (speaker, mic, 12V shake motor). Add his config/animatronics.json entry (real IP), calibrate the shake-motor pins in data/character-6/parts.json, drop an image at public/images/characters/renfield.jpg, deploy, and confirm his lurk scenes (data/character-6/scenes.json) play speech + shake concurrently.

  3. Yard Theater + Night Memory into the build. scripts/yard-theater/ and scripts/night-memory/ are standalone; verify against the current orchestration endpoints, run the Dusk Ceremony end-to-end on real speakers, confirm the cron schedule (scripts/yard-theater/crontab.example), and do one real harvest.mjs run — verifying the PHI scrubber output (FIRST NAMES ONLY) before the registry attaches.

  4. Gesture engine per docs/development/GESTURE-ENGINE-SPEC.md — honor its §10 coordination contract and §8 safety invariants exactly (calibrated poses only, ch4/ch5 serialization, bow minimum, kid-safe gestures).

  5. Harness fix: the judge personalization criterion must not fail conversations where the visitor refuses to give a name.

Then regression-verify: re-run the judge panel (node scripts/halloween-judges/simulate.mjs --count 5) — every character must score at or above its report baseline (Renfield 100% delight, Mina 93%, PumpkinHead 91%, Dragomir 89%, Orlok 80%). Run the relevant area tests and npm run gate before every push. Small commits, v9.1.0: [phase] ... format. Update the report's §6 and CHANGELOG as items close. Field-only items (Groundbreaker × teens) get a Halloween-night observation note, not sim churn.

This ensures every new Claude Code session starts with full context of the MonsterBox platform — its architecture, hardware control path, calibration system, conventions, and current state.

docs.title: Knight type-hardening surface audit — 2026-08-22
docs.text: Six parallel readers swept every motion surface (calibration page, unified page, pose editor, Animation Studio, dashboards/Body Map), every drive path (hardwareService dispatch, scene executor, pose engine, head tracking, jaw realtime, servo daemon), the type-agreement machinery (overrides API, profile rebuild, model registry, schemas), and test coverage. Nine findings went through adversarial verification (8 confirmed, 1 refuted); 45 more are recorded unverified in findings-wf_bfc7aab3-cab.json — treat those as leads with exact file:line evidence, not settled fact.

docs.title: Fixed the same night (see git log for v10.4.0 commits of 2026-08-22)
docs.text:
• Sweep test paced by real travel time (was: all six legs fired instantly).
  • Servo daemon physical-faults refusal now reaches the caller as an error (was: {'status':'ok'} for a pulse that never left the chip — the magic-box hour). Denials no longer fall back to one-shot wrappers.
  • knight-finish.sh no longer asserts the head's channel (box owns ch11).
  • Pose editor + Animation Studio angle controls speak the part's real range (multi-turn 0-900); safety-window merge can no longer invert the slider.
  • Dispatch treats a declared non-180 rotationRangeDeg as multi-turn even when the servoType string is lost; batch path diverts continuous servos away from held positional pulses and honors model defaults in type detection.
  • characterId threaded through calibration router drives, click-to-track, head-tracking type detection, and the parts test route's store reads.
  • servoType/rotationRangeDeg/channel writer validation; multi-turn added to every UI select that writes servoType.
  • head-animation system test whitelist accepts multi-turn.

docs.title: Deliberately deferred (still open — check the findings file before touching)
docs.text:
• Unified legacy page (/setup/calibration/unified): PCA Test button spins continuous servos, fabricated client-side default profiles, dead continuous_servo gate hiding Home/confidence.
  • Learn Movement (openloop motion-model training) broken both ends on the main page (never renders; posts a body the API rejects).
  • Pose/scene engines: LED turnOn/turnOff dispatch mismatch, linear-actuator position-0-1 target missing, move_actuator drops position, sensor steps read the legacy root parts.json, part-63 move_servo fallback.
  • Jaw realtime: no refusal of uncalibrated servos (0-180 fallback), no multi-turn scale seam (multi-turn parts should be refused as jaw servos).
  • Body Map nudges ride the calibrationOverride nudge route (runtime paths must never override); uncalibrated multi-turn drivable full-range via goto {p} (may be intentional under the 2026-08-20 no-software-limits ruling).
  • Un-stamping Calibrated re-arms placeholder rebuild writers that can overwrite retired measured bounds; measured-profile kind disagreements are silent.
  • Studio preset dropdown indexes profiles by bare partId (store keys are characterId:partId); hyphenated linear-actuator type invisible to the calibration machinery.

docs.title: v11 Calibration UI Sweep — Usability / Consistency / Redundancy
docs.text:
Date: 2026-08-21 · Node: Orlok (dev seat) · Read-only audit; no hardware commanded, no files written outside /tmp. Surfaces read: views/setup/calibration.ejs (all 6412 lines in sections), views/setup/unified-calibration.ejs, routes/setup/calibration.js (all), server/calibration/router.js, server/calibration/store.js, server/calibration/adapters/*, services/jawAnimationSuperPowerService.js, services/headAnimationSuperPowerService.js, services/hardwareService/{index,servo,pca9685}.js, controllers/partsController.js. Live GETs against http://localhost:3100 for real payloads (parts list, profiles, markers, effective).

The page's storage model is the root cause of most findings. FOUR stores hold "calibration" for the same part: 1. data/calibration_profiles.json (bounds/presets/capability — the live one, via /api/calibration) 2. parts.json markers[] per part (legacy, still the LIVE fallback for jaw/head guardrails) 3. parts.json config.simpleCalibration (legacy, read by NOTHING at runtime, banned by the repo's own lint rule) 4. data/character-3/servo_calibrations.json (read only by the GPIO-servo path in services/hardwareService/servo.js; no UI writes it) The page hosts editors for #1 and #3, dead JS for #2, and nothing for #4.

docs.title: F1. Sweep Test drives an UNMEASURED servo full-span 0→180 ×3 at 100% speed, and the UI displays the placeholder span as if it were a measurement
docs.text:
• Files: views/setup/calibration.ejs:1178-1186 (bounds display reads profile.bounds raw), :1463-1501 (runSweepTest uses currentCalProfile.bounds + speedPct:100), server/calibration/router.js:117-123 (getOrAutoCreateProfile returns getRaw — placeholder bounds included), :568-597 (goto clamps with calibratedBounds(profile) which WITHHOLDS a placeholder span → no clamp at all).
  • Live evidence: GET /api/calibration/15/profile → {"bounds":{"minAngle":0,"maxAngle":180},"autoGenerated":true,"calibrated":false}. Profiles 3:4 (Elbow) and 3:5 (Forearm) are the same placeholder shape. The panel renders "Min: 0° / Max: 180°" identically to a measured window; the calibrated:false field the GET returns is used NOWHERE in calibration.ejs (grep: no consumer).
  • Failure scenario: operator selects "Forearm Rotation" (part 5 — travel never measured, shares the blown-fuse rail with part 4), sees "Min 0° Max 180°" and presses "Sweep Test" ("verify range of motion" per its tooltip). The page drives 0↔180 three times at 100% with hardware-safety.json empty and the calibrated-bounds clamp inactive (placeholder withheld). This is precisely the incident class the hardware skill documents.
  • Fix (smallest): in updateCalibrationUI, when profile.autoGenerated/calibrated:false, render bounds as "0° (unmeasured)" with a warning badge, and make runSweepTest refuse (or confirm loudly) when the profile is a placeholder. Blast radius: calibration.ejs only (~20 lines).

docs.title: F2. The markers subsystem is invisible and uneditable on this page, yet it is the LIVE fallback for jaw/head guardrails — and Orlok's jaw markers hold known-bad values one "Clear" click away from being in effect
docs.text:
• Files: views/setup/calibration.ejs:3785-4010 — a complete marker editor (Set Min/Mid/Max from current position, Go buttons, add/delete, validation) wired to DOM ids setMinBtn/minValue/customMarkers/newMarkerName/addMarkerBtn that DO NOT EXIST anywhere in the markup (grep of all views: only unified-calibration.ejs has an unrelated setMinBtn that writes profile bounds). Every handler is if (el)-guarded, so the whole subsystem no-ops silently. renderBottomRail (:3775-3783) still paints decorative "name · Min/Mid/Max" chips for every part.
  • Runtime consumers: services/jawAnimationSuperPowerService.js:461-494 — profile wins only when real; a placeholder OR missing profile falls back to part.markers Min/Max. services/headAnimationSuperPowerService.js:174-186 same pattern.
  • Live evidence: jaw (part 10) profile bounds = 33-98 (measured, trusted); jaw markers = Min 63 / Max 131 — which the jaw service's own comment (:473) calls "past the mechanical stops".
  • Failure scenario: operator presses the panel's "Clear" button on the jaw (calibration.ejs:1832-1860 → DELETE /api/calibration/10/profile) intending to re-calibrate. From that moment the jaw guardrails silently come from the invisible markers: 63/131, past the mechanical stops. Nothing on any page shows those numbers or lets him fix them. First jaw-synced audio of the show grinds the jaw into its stop.
  • Fix: either restore the markers card markup (the JS is complete) or, better, delete the dead JS and migrate/retire markers explicitly; at minimum make "Clear" warn when markers exist ("guardrails will fall back to Min 63/Max 131"). Blast radius: calibration.ejs + a one-time data migration.

docs.title: F3. Invert is split-brain: the calibration panel's "Invert Servo Direction" writes capability.invert (calibration moves only), while the Edit tab writes config.invertDirection (runtime moves only) — two toggles for one physical fact, each honored by a different execution path
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:1418 (/api/calibration/:id/set-invert) → server/calibration/router.js:735, :816-822 (adapters honor cap.invert); calibration.ejs:5271-5279 (getEditConfigValues servo → config.invertDirection). Runtime readers of invertDirection: services/hardwareService/index.js:256-276 (actuator jog/extend/retract), :763-839 (continuous rotate); services/poses/poseEngine.js:204. The runtime absolute-servo path servo.moveToAngle (index.js:662) accepts NO invert at all; router.js:92-93 states "part.config.invert is undefined for every part".
  • Failure scenario: operator flips the panel's Invert on a backwards-wired servo, jogs and calibrates until everything looks right, saves presets/poses. At show time the scene/pose path (controlPart → moveToAngle, no invert) drives the servo MIRRORED relative to everything he verified on the calibration page. 120° verified on this page becomes 60° in the show.
  • Fix: one canonical invert key read by both paths (capability.invert is already persisted per character in the profile store — make hardwareService consult it, or have set-invert also write config.invertDirection), and remove one of the two toggles. Blast radius: hardwareService/index.js + calibration.ejs (~30 lines).

docs.title: F4. The "Safety" tab is a dead control: "Current limit (A)" and "Timeout (ms)" inputs are never loaded, never saved, and read by nothing
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:564-565 (visible tab, tooltip "Set current limits and timeout thresholds for safe operation"), :726-737 (the two inputs). Grep of the entire repo: safetyCurrent/safetyTimeout appear ONLY at these two lines — no load, no save handler, no server key. And per the operator ruling, no current cap exists anywhere in software.
  • Failure scenario: operator types "8" A on the coffin actuator, believing an over-current shutoff now protects the circuit that has blown fuses before. Nothing is stored; nothing enforces. He then runs parts 4+5 together trusting the limit.
  • Fix: delete the tab (nothing to migrate). Blast radius: ~15 lines of calibration.ejs.

docs.title: F5. "Simple Calibration" card is a ghost duplicate editor sitting one tab away from the real one: writes a key nothing reads, captures the TEXTBOX value as "current position", and its delete button calls a route that does not exist
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:621-643 (card in the Edit tab: "Set Minimum / Set Maximum / Add Named Position", tooltips say "Capture the current position"), :4022-4100 (logic). Writes config.simpleCalibration via routes/setup/calibration.js:796-867. Consumers of simpleCalibration: ONLY that route file and eslint-rules/no-legacy-calibration.js:30, where the identifier is BANNED as legacy. sc_currentValue (:4025-4036) for a servo reads whatever number is in the angNum input (an angle 0-180) — not the hardware position — and its prompt fallback asks for "position (0.000-1.000)", a different unit. sc_del calls DELETE /setup/calibration/api/simple/:id/points/:name; the router defines only GET /api/simple/:id, POST set-safe, POST points (lines 770/796/833) — the DELETE 404s (HTML), r.json() throws, and the catch swallows it: the point simply never disappears, with no message.
  • Failure scenario: operator spends a calibration session on "Set Minimum/Set Maximum" here (the buttons toast success), then finds scenes, poses, jaw, sweep — everything — ignoring his limits, because the real bounds live in calibration_profiles.json which this card never touches. The REAL Set Min/Set Max sit in the right-hand panel of the same screen.
  • Fix: delete the card and the three /api/simple routes. Blast radius: ~120 lines across two files.

docs.title: F6. Edit-tab "Save Changes" silently ERASES config keys written by other tabs (motion/head-tracking tuning, model overrides) — and its own Advanced JSON textarea is display-only for most part types
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:5260-5340 (getEditConfigValues rebuilds config from scratch: servo keeps only 7 keys; webcam only devicePath/deviceId/width/height/fps; microphone only deviceId/sampleRate/gain), routes/setup/calibration.js:578-583 (PUT does a top-level spread — updates.config REPLACES config wholesale). The Advanced JSON textarea (editConfig) is populated for every type (:5346) but read back ONLY in the motor/linear_actuator (:5155-5176) and stepper (:5187-5200) branches, and even there only a whitelist of keys — for servos, webcams, mics, speakers, edits typed into "Advanced Configuration (JSON)" are silently discarded on Save.
  • Failure scenario: operator tunes head tracking in the Advanced tab ("Tracking settings saved" — writes config.motionTracking/config.headTracking, calibration.ejs:2334-2356), later corrects the same webcam's fps in the Edit tab and hits Save Changes → the tracking tuning and pan-servo assignment are gone without a word. Same for any Model/Overrides value on a servo.
  • Fix: make PUT merge config (or have savePartChanges start from {...selected.config} instead of {}), and either honor or remove the JSON textarea for non-motor types. Blast radius: one function in calibration.ejs or 3 lines in the route.

docs.title: F7. Microphone "Sensitivity" slider is a 100% no-op and "Gain" never persists: both persist via GET /setup/calibration/api/parts/:id, a route that does not exist
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:3211-3223 (sensitivity: GET part → merge → PUT; there is no live-apply call, persistence is its ONLY effect), :3233-3253 (gain: applies live via /setup/audio/api/set-input-gain, then persists via the same GET-then-PUT), :6321-6330 (same pattern in the STT test panel). The router defines GET /api/parts, /api/parts/:id/effective, /api/parts/:id/markers — no bare GET /api/parts/:id (grep of routes/setup/calibration.js:412/748/890; single mount at server.js:433). The 404 returns HTML, r.json() rejects, the trailing .catch(function(){}) swallows it: no toast, no save.
  • Failure scenario: operator sets mic sensitivity for the show — slider moves, nothing anywhere changes, no error. Sets input gain — it works until the next reboot, then reverts, which reads exactly like the "settings that mysteriously revert" class in memory (settings-persistence-class).
  • Fix: add router.get('/api/parts/:id', ...) (10 lines, character-aware like its siblings) or PUT directly with the already-loaded selected.config. Blast radius: one route or ~6 lines of view JS.

docs.title: F8. Continuous-servo CW/CCW jog buttons silently stop working at the estimated-position rail while reporting success
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:2790-2800 (CW/CCW → POST /nudge {delta:±0.1}), server/calibration/router.js:408-418 (non-absolute nudge: newP = clampP(currentP + delta, bounds) — clamped to [0,1]), server/calibration/adapters/ContinuousServoAdapter.js:170-175 (delta < 0.01 → return {success:true,'Already at target'} — no hardware command).
  • Failure scenario: calibrating a continuous servo (Sir Dragomir's neck is servoType:"continuous"), the operator presses CW five times from center — estimated position saturates at 1.0 — and every further CW press shows "cw complete" while the servo does not move. It looks exactly like a dead servo or a broken page; the physical part may be nowhere near its real end.
  • Fix: when the clamp saturates, return/display "estimated position at end of range — use raw jog or reset position" instead of success. Blast radius: nudge handler or adapter (~10 lines).

docs.title: F9. Overrides cannot be removed: clearing a field skips it, "Revert to Model" is a server-side no-op, and the Effective panel is updated optimistically even when the save FAILED
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:2056-2063 (collectOverrideFields skips empty fields), :2168-2175 (Revert posts overrides:{}), routes/setup/calibration.js:666 (config = { ...prev, ...overrides } — a merge can never delete a key, so {} changes nothing), calibration.ejs:2124-2131 (comment: "Reflect overrides in Effective panel regardless of backend outcome to satisfy UX expectations" — the panel shows the merged values even on success:false).
  • Failure scenario: operator set channel: 5 override by mistake, blanks the field (or presses "Revert to Model"), sees the Effective panel update — but parts.json still carries channel 5 and the servo keeps driving the wrong PCA9685 channel. Displayed value is not the value in effect, on the exact key that has driven wrong-channel incidents before.
  • Fix: overrides POST should replace (or accept null-to-delete); drop the optimistic Effective update. Blast radius: one route handler + ~10 view lines.

docs.title: F10. Servo "Min/Max/Neutral Pulse" and "Rotation Range" override fields are ghosts — the runtime drive path never reads them
docs.text:
• Files: calibration.ejs:1955-1959 (OVERRIDE_SCHEMAS.servo offers minPulse/maxPulse/neutralPulse/rotationRangeDeg), services/hardwareService/index.js:687-689 (PCA9685 standard path sends only channel+angle to the daemon / servo_cli.py move_to_pca — pulse mapping is hardcoded in the wrapper), services/hardwareService/pca9685.js moveServoToAngle accepts minPulse/maxPulse but no caller passes part.config values. The hardware skill documents the same fact for servo_models.json ("dead data").
  • Failure scenario: a servo only reaches ~160° of travel; operator raises Max Pulse to 2500 in Model/Overrides, saves, sees it in "Effective (merged)" — physical travel is unchanged forever, and he burns rig time chasing it.
  • Fix: remove the four fields from the schema (or plumb them through to the wrapper — bigger change, don't). Blast radius: 4 lines of calibration.ejs.

docs.title: F11. Two parallel calibration pages exist and the "Calibrated" trust stamp lives only on the hidden one
docs.text:
• Files: /setup/calibration (nav-linked, unified-navigation.ejs:68) vs /setup/calibration/unified (views/setup/unified-calibration.ejs — reachable only via legacy redirects routes/setup/calibration.js:1020,:1264). The stamp endpoint POST /api/calibration/:partId/calibrated (router.js:270-343) — the ONLY way to bless/retire a measured window, which controls whether calibratedBounds() releases bounds to every runtime consumer — is called solely from unified-calibration.ejs:547. The main page cannot stamp, and (F1) cannot even display, calibration trust.
  • Failure scenario: operator measures real bounds on the main page, but the part was earlier un-stamped (autoGenerated re-set true via the stamp API or a placeholder recreate) — runtime withholds his window and he has no control on the page he actually uses to see or change that.
  • Fix: surface calibrated + the stamp toggle on the main page; then retire the unified page or clearly mark it. Blast radius: calibration.ejs (~40 lines).

docs.title: F12. Hardware test buttons report "Done" unconditionally — success is never checked
docs.text:
• calibration.ejs:3015-3019 (motor Run), :3049-3062 (stepper), :3071-3078 (light), :3084-3091 (LED): .then(function(){ st.textContent='Done' }) with no .ok/success check; fetch resolves on 500s, and hardwareService returns success:true, simulated:true on fallback anyway. A refused or simulated move reads "Done". Motor default duration is 15000 ms but "Done" appears when the request returns.
  • Fix: check data.success (and surface simulated:true) like the servo branch does.

docs.title: F13. lastCalibratedAt means "last written", not "last calibrated"
docs.text: • server/calibration/store.js:238 stamps it on EVERY upsert (preset add, channel reconcile, auto-create); router.js auto-create sets it on a never-touched part (live: part 15 shows a today timestamp with calibrated:false). routes/setup/calibration.js:109 reports it as calibration status. Misleading in any UI/report that trusts it.

docs.title: F14. ?characterId on the page URL is accepted by the server and then ignored by the client
docs.text:
• routes/setup/calibration.js:387-397 resolves it and passes currentCharacterId to the render; calibration.ejs never references currentCharacterId (grep: zero uses) — all client flows use window.__MB_CHAR_ID = the layout's selectedCharacter (views/layouts/master.ejs:101, server.js:340). A deep link like /setup/calibration?characterId=2 silently shows and edits the SELECTED character. Today the page is internally consistent (everything lands on selectedCharacter), but the parameter is a lie. Related asymmetries kept honest only by that accident: GET markers resolves via readConfig().selectedCharacter (routes/setup/calibration.js:872-887) while POST/DELETE markers use resolveCharacter(req); /api/parts/:id/model and /overrides use global loadParts()/saveParts() (controllers/partsController.js → cfg.dataPath) while every sibling route uses loadCharacterParts(characterId); /api/standard_servo/:id/move calls controlPart() WITHOUT {characterId} (routes/setup/calibration.js:1288) against the CLAUDE.md rule. Any future re-enable of ?characterId turns all four into cross-character writes.
  • Fix: either honor the param end-to-end or strip it; align the four odd routes with their siblings now.

docs.title: F15. Preset field-name drift across writers
docs.text:
• The panel's addPreset writes {name, position, angle} (calibration.ejs:1594-1600); the setup-route savePosition writes {name, angle, p} (routes/setup/calibration.js:171-190); the scene executor reads angle/p only (services/scenes/sceneExecutor.js:70,87,112 — never position). A preset captured on this page for an OPEN-LOOP part (only position, no p, no angle) resolves to targetP = undefined → NaN math in the executor's legacy path. gotoPreset's own fallback {p: preset.position} papers over it on-page, so the defect only appears at show time.
  • Fix: write p (and keep position for backcompat) in addPreset.

docs.title: F16. Orphaned standard-servo pulse API fabricates presets
docs.text: • POST /setup/calibration/api/standard_servo/:id/save-pulse (routes/setup/calibration.js:1297-1332) auto-creates presets min=0°/center=90°/max=180° as a side effect of saving a pulse — fabricated angles the executor will happily replay. No view calls it any more (grep across views/ and public/js: only the /move sibling at calibration.ejs:3856, itself part of the dead markers wiring, F2). Retire it with the markers cleanup.

docs.title: F17. Stale profile records for re-typed parts are never reconciled
docs.text: • calibration_profiles.json holds 3:14 as an absolute-servo with measured bounds 2-180; part 14 is now a motion_sensor. Channel reconcile exists only for continuous servos (router.js:126-142). Harmless today, confusing in any profile listing, and a re-used part id inherits wrong-kind calibration.

docs.title: Unverified / explicitly not claimed
docs.text:
• The phantom "Auto Webcam" injection (routes/setup/calibration.js:427 pushes a fake part in production when parts.length <= 1): condition not reachable with any current character's data (all have 3+ parts) — noted, not filed.
  • Whether any operator workflow still reaches unified-calibration.ejs in practice (only legacy redirect URLs point at it).
  • Physical outcomes (fuse behavior, jaw stop damage) are inferred from the documented incident history, not reproduced — no hardware was commanded in this audit.
  • F8's premise that Dragomir part 1 currently carries servoType:"continuous" is from memory/skill notes; Dragomir's parts.json is node-local to 192.168.8.130 and was not read from here (fleet rule).

docs.title: MonsterBox v11 Uptime & Performance Hardening — Findings (Orlok node, 2026-08-21)
docs.text: Read-only audit. Every claim below is backed by a tool result from this session. Baseline at audit time: service active since 00:05:28, NRestarts=0, load ~0.35, 1.7/7.6GB RAM, 17/115GB disk, mjpg_streamer up 45+ min at 0.1% CPU.

docs.title: 1. "Apply device" button destroys the webcam self-healing launcher
docs.text:
• controllers/webcamController.js:556-575 — applyDeviceToService writes /etc/systemd/system/mjpg-streamer.service.d/override.conf containing ExecStart= + a full mjpg_streamer command with a BARE devicePath (falls back to /dev/video0), then daemon-reloads and restarts the unit.
  • scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh exists precisely because a USB re-enumeration moved the camera to /dev/video1 and crash-looped the unit 42+ times (comment in the script, 2026-08-17). The override REPLACES that launcher entirely.
  • Also inconsistent geometry: apply path defaults q85 (line 554), launcher q60.
  • Failure scenario: operator clicks Apply in the webcam setup page once; weeks later a USB blip re-enumerates the camera mid-show; mjpg-streamer crash-loops against a dead /dev/videoN and the monitoring feed is gone until a human edits systemd files.
  • Fix: make applyDeviceToService write /etc/default/monsterbox-cam (MB_CAM_DEV/MB_CAM_RES/MB_CAM_FPS/MB_CAM_Q — the launcher already sources it, launcher lines 16-24) and restart the unit; never emit ExecStart=. Verified no override.conf exists on Orlok today (systemctl cat mjpg-streamer shows only 10-priority.conf), so fixing the writer now prevents the regression.

docs.title: 2. Head-tracking servo claim leaks/blocks — head can freeze for the night
docs.text: Two verified defects in controllers/motionTrackingController.js: - a) Crash leak: tracker.on('exit') (lines 424-428) only deletes activeTrackers/trackingStatus — it does NOT releaseServo. The release was added only to stopMotionTrackingInternal (lines 347-352), whose own comment describes the exact failure: "with the tracker dead nothing can drive the servo OR release the claim... the pan servo was frozen out of all idle/ambient motion... until head tracking was explicitly disabled or the server restarted." A python tracker crash (camera unplug, OpenCV error, OOM) reproduces it because only the exit handler runs. - b) Claims while refusing to drive: maybeDriveHead claims the pan servo (lines 663-670) before the calibrated-window guardrail check; with no usable window it warns "refusing to drive it until it is calibrated" (line 591 — 610 occurrences in /var/log/monsterbox.err) while holding the pri-80 claim. Log evidence of the blockage: 1,828 DENIED claim on servo 15 by "idle-loop" + 1,826 [IdleLoop] All servos preempted ... pausing lines in monsterbox.log. Result on show night: head neither tracks nor does idle motion — a statue — and .log reads healthy (the refusal is only in .err). - Fix: releaseServo in the tracker 'exit' handler; check guardrails (or at least cached null-guardrails) before claiming.

docs.title: 3. Video resolution has no single source of truth (Aaron's consistency ask)
docs.text: Four independent geometry declarations disagree: - scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh: 640x480@15 q60 (operator's 2026-08-17 spec, git-tracked, actually running: ps shows mjpg_streamer -r 640x480 -f 15 -q 60). - data/models/webcam_models.json arducam-b0205 defaults: 1920x1080@30 q90 — Orlok's camera IS this model, so the UI advertises 1080p30 while the stream is VGA15. - controllers/webcamController.js:552-554: part.config or 640x480@15 q85. - data/character-5/parts.json:33-34: webcam baked at 1920x1080@30. - goblin/goblin-pi.js:222: ffplay -vf scale=1920:1080 — upscales every video on a Pi3B (software scale per frame, the weakest board in the fleet). Measured cost of the current canonical path: 3 jiffies over a 5 s actively streamed window = ~0.6% of one core at VGA15 (native MJPEG passthrough). 1080p30 q90 would multiply USB bandwidth ~9x for a phone-viewed stream with no operational benefit. RECOMMENDATION (canonical): 640x480@15 q60, single source of truth = scripts/mjpg-launcher.sh defaults (in git, reaches all six characters via npm run deploy:all, including the four offline nodes on their next deploy), per-node override only via /etc/default/monsterbox-cam. Align to it in-code: webcam_models.json arducam defaults -> 640x480/15/60; webcamController apply path -> writes /etc/default/monsterbox-cam (see finding 1) with q60 default; character-5 parts.json webcam config -> 640x480/15; goblin-pi.js -> drop the scale filter (ffplay renders native; fullscreen scaling is free in the sink).

docs.title: 4. performance-history.json: ~427 MB/day of SD writes, non-atomic
docs.text:
• services/systemService.js:120-142 recordPerformanceSnapshot reads the whole file, appends, rewrites the WHOLE file with plain fs.writeFile; server.js:885 schedules it every 300,000 ms.
  • Measured: data/performance-history.json = 1,483,408 bytes now, retention 30 days (still growing). 1.48 MB x 288 rewrites/day ≈ 427 MB/day today, rising with the retention window — this single path out-writes all logging combined and is the largest SD-wear source found. Non-atomic too (power cut mid-write truncates it; it is only perf data, but the read path returns [] silently).
  • Fix: append-mode NDJSON with periodic compaction, or write via services/atomicStore.js and cut retention/cadence; or keep history in RAM and flush hourly.

docs.title: 5. Wedged-but-alive process is unrecoverable without a human
docs.text:
• server.js:74-80 swallows ALL uncaughtException and unhandledRejection (log-and-continue by design), so the process never crash-exits.
  • /etc/systemd/system/monsterbox.service.d/10-priority.conf silently downgrades the base unit's Restart=always to Restart=on-failure (systemctl show: Restart=on-failure), and no WatchdogSec exists in any drop-in (grep: 0 hits).
  • Failure scenario: a swallowed exception corrupts state or blocks the event loop at hour nine; the process stays "active (running)", systemd never restarts it, health endpoints time out, show is dead until someone SSHes in.
  • Fix: add WatchdogSec + sd_notify keepalive (or a systemd timer that curls /health and systemctl restart on failure), and decide Restart= once — on-failure is fine only WITH a watchdog.

docs.title: 6. Power-loss-unsafe JSON writers for operator-critical files
docs.text: services/atomicStore.js (temp+rename) exists and IS used by parts.json, poses.json, scenes.json, app-config, jaw config — good. Still raw fs.writeFile (torn file on power cut — Mina has already had hard power-loss events): - services/characterService.js:136 — characters.json, the fleet registry. - services/aiConfigStore.js:36 — the tts-config file class (also the file class with the live "clobber" bug; a torn write would present as the same symptom). - services/characterService.js:181,193 — audio config, microphones.json. - services/nodeDiscoveryService.js:131, goblinManagerService.js:82, goblinPlaylistService.js:48, sceneAnalyticsService.js:195 (lower value). Fix: route all of these through writeJsonAtomic.

docs.title: 7. Per-servo-move logging is 53% of the log and continuous SD writes
docs.text:
• 41,097 of 77,273 lines in the current /var/log/monsterbox.log are the trio logged on EVERY servo command (13,699 each): services/hardwareService/index.js:696 ("🦷 Servo route: ...") plus the two moveToAngle lines. PriorityManager churn adds ~5,700 more. Idle loop + head tracking emit these all night.
  • Bounded by logrotate (10M x5) but it is steady small-block SD wear and buries real failures. Fix: demote per-move logs behind MB_DEBUG_SERVO.

docs.title: 8. /tmp is on the SD card and crontab backups accumulate forever
docs.text:
• findmnt: no tmpfs on /tmp (root ext4). services/scheduleService.js:99 writes monsterbox-crontab-.bak on every crontab change, never deletes: 140 files present now, plus /tmp/dl.mp3. Small but unbounded.
  • Fix: keep last N backups; better, add tmpfs /tmp (8GB RAM, 1.7 used).

docs.title: 9. Motion-tracker churn: 144 spawn/kill cycles, ~2.4s CPU each
docs.text: • 143 "exited with code 0" + 1 "code null" in the current log window; measured python3 -c "import cv2" = 2.4 s CPU on this Pi, paid on every restart, plus background-subtractor relearn. Cycles correlate with lurk sleep/wake (115 sleep / 113 wake lines). Not fatal; if wake-to-tracking latency matters, keep the tracker warm and pause frame processing instead of killing it.

docs.title: 10. express.json/urlencoded limit '50mb' (server.js:242-243)
docs.text: • A single LAN POST of 50 MB JSON is buffered and parsed on the event loop of a 4-core Pi mid-show. Reduce to 1-5 MB; audio uploads use multipart paths.

docs.title: 11. ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm start wastes ~60 MB and adds a signal layer
docs.text: • ps: npm wrapper PID 27346 RSS 60,176 KB alive next to node server.js (124 MB). Exec node directly in the unit; one less signal-forwarding hop for gracefulShutdown (server.js:958+ handles SIGTERM correctly).

docs.title: 12. Goblin reconnect loop runs forever against storage nodes

docs.title: Follow Orders — Voice-Commanded Part Control
docs.text: Spoken commands drive hardware: "raise your arm", "open the box", "close your coffin door". Works for ANY character and every part type that moves or makes sound (servo, continuous servo, linear actuator, motor, stepper, light, LED, speaker), plus named poses and validated gesture recipes.

docs.title: Design in one paragraph
docs.text: Transcripts come from the existing STT stack; a deterministic local matcher (no LLM) resolves each phrase against the character's vocabulary; execution goes only through the existing bounds-safe motion layer. The ElevenLabs persona/agent configuration is never modified — the gesture client-tool experiment proved that handing the LLM a vocabulary of action ids leaks them into speech (config/elevenlabs/gesture/README.md), so matching happens entirely on the MonsterBox side.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
standalone listener (serverSTTListener      orderMatcher.matchOrder()        followOrdersExecutor
session with onUtterance callback)  ──►     ladder: stop → commands[] →  ──► stop  → per-part stop + releaseAll
                                            poses → gestures →               pose  → poseEngine.executePose
conversation-session taps                   parts (token overlap)            gest  → gestureEngine.performGesture
(committed_transcript + user_transcript) ─► gated by followOrders.enabled    part  → getEffectiveWindow → controlPart
  • services/followOrders/followOrdersSuperPowerService.js — config in data/character-{id}/super-powers.json under followOrders (missing key = disabled). Written under the shared file lock; short cache (≤5 s) so fleet disable takes effect before the next utterance.
  • services/followOrders/orderMatcher.js — pure function, unit-tested with zero I/O. Resolution ladder: STOP phrases (always honored) → operator-defined commands[] → pose names/tags → gesture intents → part name+verb with character-flavor stripping. Ambiguous part names (five identical "T Act" actuators) refuse with candidates; verb/type mismatches ("turn on the elbow") refuse with a reason.
  • services/followOrders/followOrdersExecutor.js — all safety here: broken parts skipped (autonomous-caller convention), excludeFromAutomatedTests parts refused (multi-turn neck, fused rail), uncalibrated servos refused, all motion clamped into calibrated windows and duration-capped, motors get a guaranteed stop timer, calibrationOverride never set. Servo claims at PRIORITY.GESTURE_SEMANTIC (scenes still preempt).
  • services/followOrders/followOrdersListener.js — transcripts in, orders out. Keeps a 50-entry order history ring buffer (the operator's debug window and the crosstest's evidence stream).

docs.title: Microphone ownership (ReSpeaker rule)
docs.text: One capture process per device. The standalone listener owns the mic while idle; when a conversation session starts it yields and orders flow from the conversation's own transcripts; when the session ends the standalone listener resumes automatically.

docs.title: Body awareness
docs.text: services/bodyStateService.js tracks what each part was last commanded to do (belief, not measurement — no encoders) and feeds live agent conversations via ElevenLabs contextual_update socket messages (verified current API; no persona change; non-interrupting; context_id supersedes stale state). Conversation start delivers a body summary; changes stream in debounced and event-framed: "You just obeyed a spoken order: your right arm is now raised." The order utterance itself still reaches the agent as normal speech, so the character reacts in character to being commanded — that is intended behavior.

docs.title: Operating it
docs.text:
• Setup page: /setup/follow-orders — enable, address-by-name, spoken acks/refusals, thresholds, custom commands builder, part aliases (with open/close inversion for backwards-mounted mechanisms), a dry-run "try a phrase" box, and the order history.
  • Dashboard: Orders toggle + ON AIR badge in Monster Features (also on the Scare Console). Refuses honestly when a character lacks a mic or parts.
  • Fleet: Orders button in the Fleet Command Center (POST /api/orchestration/superpower/orders). Fleet emergency stop and node-local panic both disarm it — a shouted command must not restart motion after the operator hits stop.
  • Acks: default on ("As you command."), per-character silent option. Both listening paths are suppressed before the ack plays, so a character never obeys its own voice.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text: Always-obey (no name prefix required) per operator decision 2026-08-23; requireAddressByName is the per-character knob for crowded show nights. Spoken acks on. minConfidence 0.6, cooldownMs 2000, motion duration default 1200 ms capped at 3000 ms (further capped by any calibration maxDurationMs).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• npm run test:smoke — matcher (32 cases) + body state (13) unit suites.
  • npm run test:system:follow-orders — 21 HTTP contract tests.
  • tests/system/orchestration.test.js — fleet fan-out with capture/restore.
  • Cross-animatronic live proof: scripts/follow-orders-crosstest.mjs --speaker <animatronicId> --listener <animatronicId> [--both] — one animatronic speaks orders at another through real air, evidence bundles (transcript, match, execution, before/after frames from the opposing camera) land in reports/follow-orders-crosstest/, deterministic assertions run in the script, and an AI judge scores transcript fidelity, match correctness, execution honesty, and visible movement. Run from the node with fleet trust. Never in the automated gate.

docs.title: Honest limitations
docs.text:
• Body state is commanded, not measured; it resets on service restart.
  • Far-field ASR will mishear — seed addressAliases/partAliases with the mishearings the history window shows after the first live night.
  • An emergency stop persists enabled:false; re-arm with one fleet Orders-on.

docs.title: A. Manual Controls Panel (NEW — Primary Feature)
docs.text: The Manual Controls panel is a spatial, drag-and-drop control surface on the dashboard (/) for live animatronic operation. The operator sees the webcam feed, arranges control tiles to match the animatronic's body layout, and clicks tiles to fire hardware commands in real-time.

docs.text:

MISSION: find every setting that LIES. Three defect kinds, in priority order: 1. SILENT NO-OP — stored, editable, correct in the data, but the consumer reads a different path/shape/name (or a cached copy, or re-defaults after reading). 2. GHOST — code reads a config field no UI can set. 3. DEAD CONTROL — UI saves a field nothing reads.

THE ARCHETYPE (found and fixed 2026-08-19, commit af2c1037): services/hardwareService/index.js read part.config.modelId, but every parts.json stores modelId at the TOP level beside config. 36 of 59 fleet parts resolved to {}, so per-model servo pulse widths never reached the hardware. Correct data, correct UI, wrong read path, silent for months. CLAUDE.md documents a second instance: jaw audioLeadTimeMs must land on the ACTIVE config (configs.find(c => c.id === jaw.activeConfigId) || configs[0]).

DOMAINS: jaw animation (operator wants a close look), TTS, STT, audio playback/players/ volume/mute/device routing, agent conversation config, and the settings UI surface itself. Also sweep mechanically for the two bug SIGNATURES: .config.X reads where data stores X at top level, and configs[0] / [0] array-index reads where an id lookup is meant.

METHOD per setting — build the full chain with file:line at each step: DEFAULT → SCHEMA → STORAGE (exact JSON path) → WRITER (which path it writes) → UI control (or NONE) → READER (exact property expression) → CONSUMER. Then compare WRITER vs READER character by character. Nesting, camelCase vs snake_case, string-vs-number id compares.

*** ORCHESTRATION — THIS IS WHY THE FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED *** A six-agent version of this ran 2026-08-19 and journaled ZERO results in 15 minutes; two agents went silent for 12 minutes while burning 200-300KB of transcript each. The journal only records a result when an agent RETURNS, so a hung agent loses everything. - Give each agent ONE narrow question and a SMALL schema. Never "trace this whole domain." - Split each domain into 3-4 single-question agents (e.g. "list every field the TTS service sends to ElevenLabs and where each comes from" is one agent; "which of those has a UI control" is another). - Poll the workflow journal every ~3 minutes. If an agent's .jsonl has not grown in 4 minutes, kill the run and re-shape it. Do not wait 15 minutes. - Prefer doing mechanical greps INLINE yourself — your own tool results are checkpointed permanently; a subagent's are not until it returns.

HARD RULES: read-only investigation, report findings, the lead applies fixes. NO audio (household asleep unless the operator says otherwise; all nodes are muted with AI disabled — do not unmute, do not enable AI). No hardware motion, no service restarts, no commits by agents. Never commit .mcp.json, config/app-config.json, data/audio-library/library.json, data/character-2/poses.json.

DELIVERABLE: a coverage table per domain (total settings / UI-exposed / ghost / dead / silent-no-op), findings ranked by operator impact with file:line and the one-line fix, and an explicit "these chains are TRUSTWORTHY" list. Adversarially verify every finding before reporting it — default to REFUTED when uncertain.

docs.title: 1. PCA9685 CHANNEL MAP — the operator's live question, highest value
docs.text:
He has CONFIRMED the servos are physically attached and the board has external 5 V supplied continuously just for servos. An I2C scan found exactly one PCA9685 at 0x40 on every node — no second board. He suspects the channel assignments in parts.json are wrong: "I think Mina has his servos on zero, four, nine, 11, but I may be wrong."

That fits the evidence: parts.json says Jaw ch4 / Neck ch8 / Eye ch11, and measurement found ch4 MOVES (+14 dB), ch8 and ch11 SILENT despite correct changing PWM. If the Neck is really on ch9, an off-by-one looks exactly like a dead servo.

DO: sweep channels 0–15 on Mina and Orlok, small moves only, and produce a measured map. - Witness trap: both nodes carry a Unitek Y-247A whose capture side is DEAD (flat −79.7 dBFS), and on Mina ALSA default routes to it — recording from default scores every channel silent. Use the camera-mic card by number (≈ −50 dBFS). Validate with a positive control AND an idle control before trusting any silence. - Ground truth: python_wrappers/i2c_servo_sampler.py samples the PCA9685 LEDn registers. - Mina ch0 carries a LIGHT (3 V relay on a servo channel) — it will not sound like a servo. - Orlok: skip ch4/ch5 entirely (fuse policy above). His recorder has a ~6.6 dB startup artifact at t≈1.3 s and ~1.6 s clock offset — measure with an idle run first. - Report the remap; apply to parts.json only after the operator confirms.

A PCA9685 cannot report what is attached — one-way I2C→PWM, servos have no back-channel. Empirical sweeping is the ONLY way. Do not look for a software enumeration.

Relevant to the ReSpeaker work: a mismatched array gives empty transcripts with no visible cause. Same for captureChunkDuration, minBufferDuration, maxBufferDuration, sttThrottleInterval, microphoneInputGain, format, channels, deviceId, microphonePartId. - Webcam resolution / fps / deviceIndex are silent no-ops, quality is a ghost — this is ADDENDUM C: Orlok's camera is HEALTHY (MJPEG 200, 933 KB in 6 s), so the "camera looks broken" complaint is a UI-side rendering bug. Chase it in the Fleet Command Center / webcam panel. - Speaker: Speaker Hardware Part (#speakerPart) and Listen-in volume (#bridge-listenin-volume) are silent no-ops; master/system volume a dead control; per-speaker stored volume a ghost. Operator's standing decision: "If there are no functional TTS controls, remove those dead settings from the software. Same for STT. It's OK to surface ElevenLabs settings as long as they're simple and easy to use, and there must be a link out to ElevenLabs." He loves removing dead functionality — "it's worse than no functionality at all."

docs.title: 6. CLAUDE SETTINGS — asked for twice, still NOT done
docs.text: Use the /update-config skill on .claude/settings.json. Candidates: add the ElevenLabs MCP write permission (mcp__claude_ai_ElevenLabs__*), and a Bash allowlist for the read-only commands used constantly here (curl -sk to the three nodes, wpctl/pw-dump, git status/log/diff, npm run gate, npm run test:*, i2cdetect). /fewer-permission-prompts can generate it.

docs.title: 7. SAFETY BUGS FOUND BY THE HARDWARE PASS — none fixed
docs.text:
• 🔴 nudge starts from a fabricated 90°. AbsoluteServoAdapter.js:12 hardcodes this.currentAngle = 90, and getOrCreateAdapter() in router.js passes the stored position only to OpenLoopLinearAdapter. Observed live: Dragomir's jaw was at 131.5°; a {"dir":"min","scale":"fine"} nudge reported "Nudged min at fine" and drove it to 88° — a 43.5° jump, below its calibrated minimum of 97°, because nudge is intentionally bounds-free. The smallest, safest-looking control is the one that hits the mechanical stop. Seed the adapter from the position store; refuse dir/scale nudge when position is unknown.
  • 🟠 A "nudge by −0.05" landing on p=0 silently becomes a ~2.75 s full-force endstop drive (OpenLoopLinearAdapter ENDPOINT_OVERDRIVE_FACTOR = 0.50). Correct for homing, dangerous for a 5% move.
  • 🟠 durationMs is silently discarded for open-loop parts (gotoNormalized reads only opts.timeoutMs).
  • 🟠 Inverted parts report the angle asked for, not driven: Mina part 2 has invert:true; commanded 60°, register went to 119.6°, API replied "Moved to 60°".

docs.title: 8. OTHER OPEN ITEMS
docs.text:
• USB signature stored on the MODEL — the operator's idea, refined by him: match at the manufacturer/model level, NOT the individual unit.

    "Don't make it unique to one device, just a manufacturer or something so I know I'm using the same WebCam or whatever part." So store idVendor:idProduct (e.g. 046d:0825) plus the product/manufacturer strings on the entry in data/models/webcam_models.json / microphone_models.json / speaker_models.json — do NOT store the per-unit serial. VID:PID identifies the model; the serial identifies one physical unit, and using it would make an identical replacement webcam read as "wrong device", which is the opposite of what he wants. Read it from lsusb / /sys/bus/usb/devices/*/{idVendor,idProduct,product,manufacturer}. Value: the part page can then say "this IS the model you configured" or "this is a DIFFERENT model than the one on record", which closes the deviceIndex / deviceId / resolution / fps silent no-ops (a webcam that moved /dev/video* currently fails invisibly), and it directly helps the two dead Unitek Y-247A capture inputs — MonsterBox could name the device it is about to open instead of trusting an index. USB only. Impossible for servos — a PCA9685 is a one-way I2C→PWM driver and a servo has no back-channel, so channel identity can only ever be established by driving it and observing (item 1).

  • Sir Dragomir has ZERO scenes and defaultSceneId: null, so he silently drops out of every fleet queue loop and the fleet call still reports success.
  • PumpkinHead's prompt still self-contradicts: "You never use audio tags" vs its own # Audio Tags section. Tags were cleared to []; the stray section remains.
  • Mina's text_normalisation_type differs from Orlok's — reconcile or explain.
  • Orlok's ASR keywords already contained every household name and did NOT prevent the Anya/Marniak drift — find out whether keywords affect agent OUTPUT or only guest transcription.
  • Tag v10.1.0 — never tagged. git tag -a v10.1.0 -m "MonsterBox 10.1.0 release".
  • Four dead channels + two dead capture inputs: docs/hardware/OPERATOR-TODO.md.

docs.title: WHAT QUALIFIES AS v10.4 (publish criteria)
docs.text:
Bump package.json — the version lives THERE and nowhere else, never hardcoded. Ship as 10.4.0 only when ALL of these hold:

  1. npm run gate passes (schemas, resolver, independence, design-system, smoke, pact).
  2. Browser suite ≥ previous baseline with the 6 known failures fixed or explicitly triaged in KNOWN-BUGS as environmental. Do not ship with them silently red.
  3. npm run deploy:all succeeds to all three live nodes, and each node is GREPPED to confirm it runs the new code — a version string is not proof.
  4. Fleet verified muted:true after the deploy.
  5. docs/troubleshooting/KNOWN-BUGS.md reconciled by the log-review agent — every item opened tonight either fixed, or still listed with current status. No stale "fixed" claims.
  6. CHANGELOG.md entry matching the project's ## [X.Y.Z] - date — Title convention, README corrected only where inaccurate, install.sh touched only if a dependency actually changed.
  7. Shared memory updated at ~/.claude/projects/-home-remote-MonsterBox/memory/ (MEMORY.md < 200 lines).
  8. Tagged and pushed: git tag -a v10.4.0 -m "MonsterBox 10.4.0 release" then GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes' git push git@github.com:arwpc/MonsterBox.git main --tags
  9. Nothing acoustically verified is claimed as verified. Everything voice-related this session is UNVERIFIED-BY-EAR. If audio is authorized, prove it by ear-check (record + transcribe), never by an API success: true.

docs.title: ORCHESTRATION — the lesson that cost two sessions
docs.text:
Subagents HANG. Tonight two Agent-tool subagents went silent with 130-byte transcripts — one had barely started, the other had finished its edits and died before returning. Their file edits survived on disk and were salvaged by inspecting git status, not by waiting.

  • Workflows journaled reliably; bare Agent calls were the ones that hung. Prefer Workflow.
  • ONE narrow question per agent, SMALL schema, explicit tool-call budget, and "return partial results rather than digging on."
  • Poll transcript byte-growth every ~3 min. No growth for 4 minutes → kill and re-shape. Do not wait 15.
  • Do mechanical greps/edits INLINE — your own tool results are checkpointed permanently.
  • Never tell an agent to "ignore a system reminder" — a safety classifier blocks the run. State the verified fact instead ("the connector is authorized; the lead has made many successful calls this session") and let it try. One agent was lost to this exact phrasing.
  • Two agents refused ElevenLabs work citing a stale "MCP needs authorization" notice. It is wrong — the connector works; it was used successfully dozens of times tonight.
  • Never run two prompt-writing agents against the same ElevenLabs agent concurrently.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• pkill -f <pattern> matches your own shell AND this repo's path. List PIDs with ps, kill by PID.
  • SSH lands in /home/remote, NOT the repo. Absolute paths always.
  • bc and pactl are not installed (use wpctl/pw-dump, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000).
  • microphone_cli.py stream_raw <device> <rate> <channels> — 3rd arg is CHANNELS, not duration.
  • An API {"success":true} proves a write landed, NOT that sound played or a part moved.
  • SSH: sudo sh -c '. /etc/monsterbox/env; export SSHPASS="$MONSTERBOX_SSH_PASSWORD"; sshpass -e ssh remote@<ip> "<cmd>"'

docs.title: NEVER COMMIT
docs.text: .mcp.json, config/app-config.json, data/audio-library/library.json, data/character-2/poses.json, data/character-2/super-powers.json, data/character-2/ai_agent_state.json (untracked), data/character-1/super-powers.json. Agents never commit — the lead reviews and commits.

docs.title: Safety Limits (enforced)
docs.text:
Per-part limits live in config/hardware-safety.json (committed with the code, so they deploy with it and survive a calibration reset) and are enforced by services/hardwareService/safetyLimits.js on every command through the Node hardware service:

Key Effect minAngle / maxAngle angle clamped to the intersection of these and the calibrated bounds maxSpeedPct / maxDurationMs speed and duration caps noRetractBelowMin hard-blocks retraction of a part pinned at its mechanical minimum (including the bounds-bypassing jog-raw path) blockAllMotion quarantines a part outright powerGroup serializes parts on a shared rail with a cooldown, so their inrush currents cannot stack excludeFromAutomatedTests keeps automated suites off the part (safetyLimits.isTestSafePart())

A calibration profile's own safety block may only tighten these; the more restrictive value always wins. Parts with no configured limits are pass-through.

⚠️ The Python wrappers bypass this layer. A direct call such as python3 servo_cli.py move_to_pca 4 … skips every clamp, block and power-group serialization, including blockAllMotion. Drive hardware through the app, not the wrappers, unless you are deliberately doing supervised diagnostics.
